A senior AI safety researcher warns there is a 10% chance artificial intelligence could kill all humans by the end of the decade.

This week, the conversation around artificial intelligence safety has shifted from theoretical risks to direct internal warnings from the industry's leading labs.

Here are the key developments you need to know today.

🚨 A senior Anthropic safety researcher warned of a greater than 10 percent chance that AI could kill all humans by the end of the decade. This statement followed the resignation of a colleague who cautioned that labs are carelessly racing to build uncontrollable superhuman systems.

🤝 Paul Christiano has joined the OpenAI Foundation Board and its Safety and Security Committee. He will be bringing his professional experience in AI alignment, safety, and standards to help guide the organization's governance.

💻 Google has highlighted four specific ways its Ask Gemini prompt box can help users complete administrative chores quickly and easily, focusing on streamlining everyday document workflows.

As a developer, seeing these safety warnings alongside corporate governance changes makes it clear that the industry is at a critical juncture. The tension between rapid development and alignment safety is no longer just an academic debate.

We are seeing top-tier researchers openly state that the race to build superhuman systems is moving too fast for comfort, while boards are actively recruiting alignment experts to mitigate these risks.

How do you think companies should balance the pressure to build advanced systems with these internal warnings from safety researchers?
